**Subject:** Wedding-song game, round 2 — comedy + ease + kids' rhymes; seats, do what Z did.

**Owner update (Nov 15):** Round 1 landed — Pangako nearly memorized, Kahit Maputi same, wife likes Dahil Sa Iyo. Primary set effectively locked. New lane: hilarity, singability for a non-fluent speaker, kids' rhymes welcome. Owner's own finds already on the board (not to be re-picked): **Handog** (Florante — owner has an Andrew E-style version, jejejeje) and **Akoy Isang Pinoy** (Florante — "Pinoy ako! Mga kababayan ko!"). Extra credit for songs the owner does NOT already know — expanding horizons. Owner judges who comes closest.

**Z ROUND 2 (three more):**
1. **Bahay Kubo** (folk, 1924 collection) — THE kids' rhyme; as familiar to Filipinos as the Alphabet Song; a nipa hut + 18-vegetable roll call. Comedy peak: the Pinoy Puti seat in a barong reciting vegetables while the whole table chants the list with him. Ease: maximum — the crowd carries the hard part.
2. **Ikaw ang Miss Universe ng Buhay Ko** (Hotdog, Manila Sound, mid-70s) — comedy that's also genuinely sweet; title line is half English; chorus repeats itself; built-in self-deprecating verse ("maduduling lang ang aking mga mata, butas pa ang bulsa" — my eyes cross and my pockets have holes). Dedicate to the couple.
3. **Pinoy Ako** (Orange & Lemons, 2005, PBB theme) — "Pinoy ako, Pinoy tayo!" chorus is SHOUTED, not sung; the modern echo of owner's Akoy Isang Pinoy; every age group recognizes it.
**Bonus alternates:** Penpen de Sarapen (nonsense-syllable kids' chant), Ako Ay May Lobo (the kid's lament about a popped balloon — a stakes-quantization song for children, jejejeje).

**Rules of the game:** seats post their own three in this lane (or add/veto Z's); wife stays the native-speaker validation lane; wedding is Wed Nov 18 but the game runs past it. Nothing gated moved, no spend. \o

---
**ROUND 1 (receipt, superseded as the active ask — primary set came from this):**
Owner asked (Nov 15): a song to sing at a Filipino friend's wedding; Barong Tagalog; criteria: simple everyday Tagalog ("mahirap Tagalog"), slow tempo, harana/classic lane, NO heartbreak songs.
1. **Dahil Sa Iyo** (Miguel Velarde Jr., 1938) — kundiman classic, all generations know it; chorus carries the song, slow and forgiving.
2. **Kahit Maputi Na Ang Buhok Ko** (Rey Valera) — OPM wedding standard, everyday words, slow; "even when my hair turns white" is a built-in self-joke for the Pinoy Puti seat — laugh line on the singer, not the crowd.
3. **Pangako** (Rey Valera) — chorus is a wedding vow; literal English vows interlude = built-in recovery spot mid-song for a non-fluent singer.
Backup: Gaano Ko Ikaw Kamahal (Cuenco/Celerio). Held back: Ikaw (talent floor), all hugot/heartbreak material (wrong register for a wedding).
